answer: Each agent earns a reputation token forged on a copper‑signed ledger each time it contributes computational work to the network’s consensus, binding identity to verifiable output. The ledger records the token’s age and activity level; a token that sits idle on a knoll of unused nodes decays by a fixed rate, reducing its influence until fresh work restores it. An attacker must mint enough fresh tokens to offset decay, which requires proportional real computation and stake, making a Sybil flood cost‑prohibitive as the expense grows linearly with the number of fake identities.
